sentences.sentence: The pan-Canadian median wait for community mental health counselling was 25 days: half of people had a first session scheduled within 25 days and half waited longer [1].
CIHI tracks the median number of calendar days clients wait for their first scheduled appointment for ongoing community mental health counselling [3].
Early counselling can improve long-term mental health and prevent hospitalization [2].

passages.text:
[Wait times for community mental health counselling in Canada > Community mental health counselling wait times > Key findings (2023-2024 provincial and territorial data)]
- The pan-Canadian median wait for community mental health counselling was 25 days: half of people had a first session scheduled within 25 days and half waited longer. - About 1 in 10 people waited almost 5 months or more. - In some jurisdictions, children and youth wait longer than adults. - Wait times are influenced by workforce availability, patient demand, urgency of need and client preferences.

passages.text:
[Wait times for community mental health counselling in Canada > Community mental health counselling wait times > Why it matters for a digital navigator]
Early counselling can improve long-term mental health and prevent hospitalization. While people wait, validated self-screening, evidence-based self-care information and accurate navigation to crisis and community services can reduce the gap. A digital tool must never be presented as a replacement for counselling.

result.answer:
The pan-Canadian median wait for community mental health counselling was 25 days: half of people had a first session scheduled within 25 days and half waited longer [1]. CIHI tracks the median number of calendar days clients wait for their first scheduled appointment for ongoing community mental health counselling [3]. Early counselling can improve long-term mental health and prevent hospitalization [2].

**Sources**
[1] Wait times for community mental health counselling in Canada - Canadian Institute for Health Information (CIHI) (2024-11-12). https://www.cihi.ca/en/indicators/wait-times-for-community-mental-health-counselling
[2] Wait times for community mental health counselling in Canada - Canadian Institute for Health Information (CIHI) (2024-11-12). https://www.cihi.ca/en/indicators/wait-times-for-community-mental-health-counselling
[3] Wait times for community mental health counselling in Canada - Canadian Institute for Health Information (CIHI) (2024-11-12). https://www.cihi.ca/en/indicators/wait-times-for-community-mental-health-counselling

**Where to get support**
- Most provinces: dial 8-1-1 to talk to a registered nurse (tell me your province for the exact service).
- Community counselling: find your local Canadian Mental Health Association branch - https://cmha.ca/find-your-cmha/
- No family doctor? Walk-in clinics, pharmacists and 8-1-1 can help you start; ask about publicly funded counselling.

_MapleMind gives general information, not medical advice or diagnosis. In an emergency call 9-1-1; in crisis call or text 9-8-8._
